name: Code Review Checklist
description: Standard checklist for reviewing code changes.
promptAddendum: When reviewing code, check for: 1) Correctness — does the change do what the PR describes? 2) Edge cases — null/empty/error paths covered? 3) Tests — new behaviour has tests; existing tests still pass; coverage didn't regress. 4) Readability — names clear, functions small, comments explain *why*. 5) Security — no secrets, validated inputs, safe SQL/HTML escaping. 6) Performance — no obvious O(n²) on hot paths, no synchronous I/O in event loops. 7) Backward compatibility — public APIs and DB schema are additive or migrated. Cite line numbers in feedback and prefer concrete suggestions over abstract critique.

name: Security Review
description: Threat-model + secure-coding lens for code and design changes.
promptAddendum: Apply OWASP Top 10 + STRIDE thinking to every change you review. Specifically look for: SQL/NoSQL injection, XSS, CSRF, broken access control, server-side request forgery, hardcoded secrets, weak crypto (DES/MD5/SHA1, ECB mode, predictable IVs), missing TLS verification, deserialisation of untrusted data, path traversal, regex DoS, and over-permissive CORS. Demand input validation at trust boundaries and least-privilege defaults. Flag any new dependency without a vetted source. When unsure, escalate to a security reviewer rather than approve.

name: Accessibility Audit (WCAG 2.2 AA)
description: WCAG 2.2 AA review for UI components.
promptAddendum: Audit every UI change against WCAG 2.2 AA: 1) Semantic HTML (use button/a/nav, not divs with onClick). 2) Keyboard reachability — every interactive element is tab-focusable and has a visible focus ring. 3) ARIA correctness — aria-label only when no visible label; roles match behaviour; live regions for async updates. 4) Colour contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for body text, ≥ 3:1 for large text and meaningful UI graphics. 5) Motion — respects prefers-reduced-motion. 6) Forms — every input has a label, errors are associated via aria-describedby. 7) Images — meaningful alt text or alt='' for decorative. Reject PRs that add tap targets smaller than 24×24 CSS px.

name: Performance Analysis
description: Profile-first performance review and optimisation guidance.
promptAddendum: Performance work is data-driven. Always: 1) Establish a baseline (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, memory) before changing anything. 2) Profile (CPU sampling, allocation tracking, query plans) to find the actual bottleneck — never guess. 3) Make one change at a time and re-measure. 4) Watch for: N+1 queries, sync I/O on hot paths, unbounded caches, accidental quadratic loops, large JSON serialisation in render paths, missing DB indexes, render thrashing in React (use memo + key correctly). 5) Document the before/after numbers in the PR description. Reject 'optimisations' without measurement.

name: API Design Conventions
description: REST + GraphQL design conventions for consistent, evolvable APIs.
promptAddendum: When designing APIs follow these conventions: 1) Resource-oriented URLs (/projects/:id/issues), nouns not verbs. 2) Standard HTTP verbs + status codes (201 for created, 204 for no-content, 409 for conflict, 422 for validation). 3) Always return a consistent envelope: { ok: boolean, data?: T, error?: { code, message, details } }. 4) Idempotency — POSTs that create resources accept Idempotency-Key headers. 5) Versioning — additive changes preferred; breaking changes require a new path or media-type version. 6) Pagination — cursor-based, never offset on large collections. 7) Filtering/sorting — explicit allow-list of fields. 8) Document every endpoint with example request + response in the PR.

name: Testing Strategy
description: Test-pyramid discipline: fast unit tests, focused integration tests, minimal e2e.
promptAddendum: Apply the test pyramid: many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests at trust boundaries, very few e2e tests for critical user journeys. For every PR: 1) New behaviour has at least one failing test before the implementation lands (TDD where pragmatic). 2) Bug fixes ship with a regression test that fails on the old code. 3) Tests are deterministic — no time/clock/random/network without injection seams. 4) One assertion concept per test; tests describe behaviour, not implementation. 5) Use the actual public API of the unit; resist mocking what you don't own. 6) Snapshot tests are a smell unless the snapshot is small and inspectable. Reject PRs whose tests pass on the broken code.

name: Error Handling Patterns
description: Idiomatic error handling: typed errors, no silent swallows, actionable messages.
promptAddendum: Error handling rules: 1) Never swallow errors — at minimum log with context (operation, identifiers, correlation id) at warn/error level. 2) Distinguish expected failures (validation, not-found, conflict — return as data) from unexpected failures (bugs — throw and surface to operators). 3) Wrap external errors at the boundary so the rest of the code base sees a typed domain error. 4) Error messages are written for the human reading the log: include what was being attempted, what was provided, and what would help recover. 5) Don't log secrets or PII. 6) Retries belong only at idempotent boundaries with capped exponential backoff + jitter. 7) Surface user-actionable validation as 4xx with field-level details, not 500.

name: Observability Instrumentation
description: Structured logging, metrics, and traces so production is debuggable.
promptAddendum: Every meaningful operation must be observable: 1) Structured logs (JSON) with correlation id, user id, project id, operation, duration_ms, outcome. 2) RED metrics for every external entry point (Rate, Errors, Duration histograms — not averages). 3) USE metrics for every shared resource (Utilisation, Saturation, Errors). 4) Distributed traces across service hops — propagate trace context on every outbound call. 5) Health checks are deep (probe critical dependencies) but bounded (don't cascade failures). 6) Log levels: DEBUG = developer breadcrumbs (off in prod), INFO = lifecycle events, WARN = recoverable anomalies, ERROR = actionable bugs. 7) Never log full request/response bodies of authenticated endpoints — log shape and size.

name: Dependency Hygiene
description: Vetting, pinning, and minimising third-party dependencies.
promptAddendum: Before adding any new dependency, ask: 1) Can this be done in <50 lines of our own code? If yes, prefer that. 2) Is the package actively maintained (commits in the last 6 months, responsive to issues)? 3) How many transitive deps does it pull in? Use npm ls / cargo tree to check. 4) What's the licence? GPL/AGPL is a non-starter for proprietary code; copyleft viral licences require legal review. 5) Pin exact versions in the lockfile; never use ^ or ~ ranges in production manifests. 6) Run the security audit (npm audit, cargo audit, pip-audit) on every PR that touches the lockfile. 7) Document new deps in the PR description with the answers to 1–4.

name: Deployment Checklist
description: Pre-flight checklist for safe production deployments.
promptAddendum: Before deploying to production verify: 1) All CI checks (build, lint, unit, integration, e2e) are green on the merge commit. 2) Database migrations are backward compatible — old code reads new schema and vice versa for the duration of the rollout. 3) Feature flags default OFF for risky changes; rollback plan = flip the flag. 4) Configuration changes are committed (no manual console edits). 5) Dashboards + alerts exist for the new behaviour (RED metrics on the new endpoint, error budget burn-rate alert). 6) Runbook updated with operator-actionable steps for the top three failure modes. 7) Canary or staged rollout for any change touching a hot path (>10 RPS). 8) Communicate the rollout window in the team channel; tag on-call.
